title: paper: scope claims to what is actually implemented, not to what D describes
description: Provisional D describes quarantined inference with governed promotion as a headline aspect. camayoc-s0h says quarantine planes are design-only — inferred facts are not routed to a low-trust plane — and camayoc-mip says promotion out of crew:inferred is unimplemented. A patent may claim constructively reduced embodiments; a systems paper may claim only what is built and measured. Before any drafting, produce the implemented set: for each D aspect (provenance-refusing ingress, quarantine, governed promotion, falsifier-gated verification, liveness by deliberate absence, installation-time gate proof, tier-honest serving, typed non-answers), state built / partial / design-only with the code path or the bead that says otherwise. Anything not built is future work or is cut. Getting this wrong is the fastest way to an unrecoverable review.
acceptance_criteria: A table of D's aspects against implementation status, each row citing a code path or an open bead. The paper's claims are drawn only from the built rows.
close_reason:
Done. docs/design/implemented-set.md states, per D aspect, built / partial / design-only with the code path or the bead that says otherwise. Measured against the source at this commit, not carried from a bead — each row produced by grepping for the mechanism OUTSIDE docs/ and competency/, since a term appearing only in design prose is design-only by definition. That method is what classified aspects 2 and 3.

Result: three built, three partial, two design-only.
BUILT — provenance-refusing ingress (sourceKind mandatory + closed vocabulary at shapes/code-entities.ttl:50, refusal tested in tests/test_knot_provenance.py); falsifier-gated verification (shapes/core.shapes.ttl:85-89); installation-time gate proof (scripts/gate_probe.sh + tests/test_gate_probe.py).
DESIGN-ONLY — quarantined inference and governed promotion, exactly as camayoc-s0h and camayoc-mip say. This is the critical finding: D discloses that pairing as the PRIMARY contemplated embodiment, so a paper inheriting D's framing describes a system that does not exist.

THE AUDIT SURFACED A GAP THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE, and camayoc-102 needs it. The competency suite is 47 questions (sha256:7a0cc4abad386885); the repo holds FOUR stored queries, all in the metrics slice. Written into the paper plan as the critical path.

title: paper: write up the 2026-08-06/07 incident night as the empirical core
description: competency/verification-and-liveness.md records a measured incident night on a live crew: ELEVEN separate instances of a check that could not have failed, and four separate beads describing one root cause. It is already taxonomized — a guard documented as belt-and-braces that was the only mechanism; a byte-identity test that passed against a read-write open; a schema check comparing (type, name) only, so ADD COLUMN was invisible; a binding condition whose two branches were the same function; a grep -c matching the description of the bug in the test payload; a grep against an empty capture whose 0 was read as absent; a corroboration equally consistent with both competing hypotheses. Most papers about verification integrity have no field data at all. This is the paper's strongest asset and it is sitting in a competency-question doc. Turn it into a labeled corpus with the taxonomy as categories. Two things it needs to survive review: how instances were identified (selection bias is the obvious attack — were these found by looking for them, and what was the denominator), and a RATE rather than a count, since eleven of eleven checks examined and eleven of four hundred are different papers.
acceptance_criteria: A labeled corpus with per-category counts, a stated identification method, and a denominator.
close_reason:
Done. docs/design/incident-corpus.md turns competency/verification-and-liveness.md into a labelled corpus with the taxonomy as categories: A1-A7 for verification integrity, each with what was checked, what was claimed, and the ADJACENCY between them; category B for the four-mechanisms-one-missing-predicate liveness family; category C for armed-not-running.

The move that makes it paper material: the falsifier question is applied mechanically to all seven forms, and it separates all seven from verification without hindsight. A1/A4 could not fail at all. A5/A7 return 'confirmed' under the negation of the claim. A2/A6 are SOUND CHECKS RUN OUTSIDE THEIR PRECONDITIONS rather than bad checks — which preserves the distinction competency question 5 exists to protect, and which a naive reading of the corpus would flatten. A3 is the insidious one: a falsifier scoped NARROWER than the claim, so the check works sometimes, and it is where the mandatory falsifier field visibly earns its keep, because a human writing 'renamed or retyped column' into that field has in that act noticed ADD COLUMN is uncovered.

BOTH ATTACKS THE BEAD NAMED ARE ANSWERED IN THE DOC, IN THE PAPER RATHER THAN AN APPENDIX.

Selection bias: partly sought, and it says so. The category B family was NOT sought — four P1s collided and the common cause was noticed, closer to a census than a search. Category A was partly sought: the first instance was incidental, and once found the crew began asking the falsifier question of other checks. So the corpus supports 'when we asked what would have falsified each check, checks failed that question at a rate that surprised us, across seven distinct forms' and does NOT support 'N% of verifications in this codebase are unfalsifiable'. The paper must make exactly the first claim.

Rate: THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT RECOVERABLE from the record as kept, and the doc states that instead of estimating one. Total verifications that night was never counted; per-form counts were not recorded; crew size and agent-hours are absent, so no normalisation. The one genuine rate in the corpus is category B at 4 OF 4 — every routing mechanism examined lacked the liveness predicate, a complete census of a small enumerable population with no selection step — and that is what the paper should lead with when a rate is demanded, presented for exactly what it is.

Section 5 specifies the instrumentation that would fix it prospectively: count accepted vs falsifier-refused verifications at ingress (the refusal count IS the rate, measured without a search step), record the A1-A7 form on refusals, normalise by agent-hours from the cost-accounting slice, which is already a deterministic-parser fact off local session files. Noted in one sentence and no more that the proposed mechanism is also the instrument that would have measured the problem it was built for — overselling that would be its own unfalsifiable claim.

Stating the gap rather than papering over it is not a concession here; a paper arguing that claims must name what would falsify them cannot make an unfalsifiable claim about its own evidence.

title: paper: execute the competency questions as named stored queries and report coverage
description: competency/verification-and-liveness.md sets its own rule: 'every question must eventually run as a named stored query (quipu #79)'. Competency questions are the standard evaluation methodology for ontology and knowledge-graph work, and executed ones are the difference between a design document and a results section. This is the paper's evaluation. Report per-question: does a stored query exist, does it return, and does it return something a human agrees with. A question that cannot be expressed as a query is itself a finding — it means the ontology does not carry the terms the question needs, which is exactly what camayoc-b6h calls a competency gap.
acceptance_criteria: Every competency question in the three files is either a named stored query with a result, or is recorded as an ontology gap with the missing term named.
close_reason:
Done, and the chore turned into the finding. Reported per question by scripts/query_coverage.py (just query-coverage); executed by tests/test_competency_queries.py against tests/fixtures/verification-liveness.ttl.

COVERAGE OF THE VERIFICATION-AND-LIVENESS SLICE: 5 OF 13, verdict Partial. Before this the slice had ZERO stored queries — all four in the repo served the metrics slice.

The real result is not the count. ONLY FIVE OF THE THIRTEEN QUESTIONS CAN BE EXPRESSED AT ALL with today's vocabulary. The other eight name terms the ontology does not carry, so they are competency gaps in exactly the sense camayoc-b6h defines — an ontology gap surfaced as its own outcome, never answered from the nearest term. Each gap is reported with the terms it would need, and a test fails any gap that does not name them, because a gap without them is a complaint rather than a finding.

STORED AND EXECUTING: Q1 falsifier-for-a-verification, Q2 verifications with no falsifier, Q10 blockers by evidence kind, Q11 execution path for a mechanism, Q13 single-principal-owned paths.

GAPS, with what each needs: Q3 no verifiedAt and no relation to the change a check followed; Q4 nothing records that a check was PROVEN adversarial rather than asserted — the very property camayoc-104 just established for the gate probes, which the ontology cannot state about anything else, and that is a good honest paragraph for the paper; Q5 no relation from a check to the variable under test, costing us in both directions since that question exists to protect valid adjacent-setting evidence; Q6 and Q8 no Principal and no observed liveness record to join against — correctly NOT a stored fact per ingress rule 5, but a read-time join needs something to join TO, and this is the largest gap because it blocks the four-beads-one-cause family the paper leads with; Q7 no blockedOn edge; Q9 no state transitions; Q12 no digest on either side of an execution path.

Q2 has a subtlety worth recording: a Verification without a falsifier CANNOT be written through a gated ingress, so Q2's population is precisely the store's pre-gate legacy and it correctly returns nothing against a store that was always gated. The fixture seeds two pre-gate rows so the query is proven able to find them. That resolves the apparent tension with the competency doc's acceptance criterion demanding a non-empty Q2.

THE SUITE'S OWN ACCEPTANCE DISCIPLINE IS HONOURED: every query runs against a fixture seeded with BOTH arms, a positive finding and a control negative, because 'an empty result without those arms is not proof that the fleet is healthy'. Where a query finds bad rows, a second test asserts the healthy rows are excluded — a query returning everything would pass a bare non-empty assertion. Coverage itself is machine-checked rather than asserted: the reporter fails a query naming a predicate the ontology does not define (it would return zero rows forever and read as 'nothing to report'), fails a question claiming a query absent from disk, and the 5/13 figure is pinned by a test so the paper's number cannot drift.

Proven non-vacuous, per this repo's own rule. Two sabotages, both confirmed red: dropping Q2's FILTER NOT EXISTS so it returns every verification fails the discriminating arm; repointing a query at an undefined predicate fails the grounding check.

Suite 65 passed (was 52), just check 0 issues. Executed with rdflib and skipped when absent, matching the existing quipu-server pattern — these prove the QUERIES, not the store.

NOT DONE, and it is now the only open build decision in the paper plan: closing any of the eight gaps. Q6/Q8 is the one that changes what the paper's section 4 can claim; the rest can ship as future work. That is a keeper call and is recorded as step 6 of the build order.

title: paper: write docs/design/paper.md — the admission leg of the SARC program
description: House style, following quipu docs/design/paper.md and yupana docs/design/paper.md. The thesis is camayoc's README line: how knowledge earns its way into the graph, so the store never has to trust an extractor. Positioning is unusually clean and should be stated up front: this is the third leg of a three-paper program. quipu compiles SARC into the store (submitted, arXiv:submit/7961151); yupana compiles it into the action; camayoc governs admission — what may enter at all. The nearest external anchor is SARC-DQ, which quipu's own related-work section describes as gating evidence quality, and evidence quality is precisely camayoc's territory rather than yupana's. TrustGraph is the named foil already in docs/vision.md: bolt an extraction pipeline onto the store and the answer to 'why should I believe this fact' is 'a model wrote it during ingestion'.
acceptance_criteria: A plan doc with thesis, contributions, evaluation design, scope boundaries, and explicit positioning against the quipu and yupana papers.
close_reason:
Done. docs/design/paper.md written in the house style, following quipu's and yupana's plan docs, with the implementation-status banner the repo convention requires.

Thesis is the README line sharpened: a knowledge store that accepts machine-written facts has a trust problem it cannot solve internally, because by the time a fact is in the store the question 'why should I believe this' has already been answered badly — so the answer must be a REFUSAL AT ADMISSION, not a confidence score at read time. The second half is what makes it a paper rather than a design note: the refusal must itself be falsifiable. Anyone can add a mandatory provenance tag; the contribution is applying the same standard to the checks themselves.

Positioning is stated up front as the bead asked. Three-paper program worded identically to yupana's plan (quipu compiles SARC into the store, submitted; yupana into the action; camayoc governs admission), with SARC-DQ as the nearest external anchor and the one-sentence justification for why the admission leg is its own paper — quipu's own related-work describes SARC-DQ as gating evidence quality, and evidence quality is camayoc's territory rather than yupana's. TrustGraph is the named foil from docs/vision.md and opens the paper, with a note to be fair to it: the integrated approach has real ergonomic advantages and the paper is stronger for conceding that before arguing the trade is wrong for agent-written knowledge specifically.

Five contributions (C1 provenance-refusing ingress, C2 falsifier-gated verification, C3 the incident corpus, C4 installation-time gate proof, C5 liveness by deliberate absence as a POSITION not a mechanism), each annotated with its state from implemented-set.md. Ten-section outline, build order, and an explicit 'what this paper is not'.

The section that matters most is section 5, the evaluation, and it is honest rather than managed: coverage is 4 of 47 competency questions, all four in the metrics slice, ZERO in the verification-and-liveness slice the corpus is about. So the corpus MOTIVATES a capability rather than demonstrating one, and a reviewer asking 'could your system have answered these on the night' gets a no. Three routes given, camayoc-102 recommended and marked the critical path — it is the only item in the whole plan that requires building rather than writing.

title: paper: prove the gate probe adversarially, not just that it passes
description: camayoc-045 closed by giving the installer's gate proofs real refusal tests in CI (tests/test_gate_probe.py). The claim in provisional D is stronger than 'the probes pass': it is that each probe omits exactly one required property SO THAT THE ARMS DISCRIMINATE, and a failure of one gate cannot make another look enforced. That is a claim about independence and it is not established by a green suite. Break each gate individually and confirm only the matching probe flips. This is the same discipline yupana calls non-vacuity — a green check that cannot go red is asserting nothing — and it is the paper's own thesis applied to its own installer, which is worth a sentence in the write-up.
acceptance_criteria: A mutation-style test per gate showing that disabling gate N flips probe N and no other.
close_reason:
Done. The independence claim is now attacked from both ends and both attacks are proven able to fail.

WHAT WAS MISSING. ArmIndependenceTests already proved each arm is REACHABLE and can report acceptance on its own. That is not D's claim. D claims each probe omits EXACTLY ONE required property so the arms discriminate, and a failure of one gate cannot make another look enforced. Every pre-existing test passes just as happily if two probes violate the same shape, because every one of them ran against a store that answers all four probes identically — such a store cannot distinguish 'the gate works' from 'something refuses everything'.

STATIC HALF — ProbeDiscriminationTests. Parses sh:minCount 1 paths per sh:targetClass out of shapes/core.shapes.ttl and the probe payloads out of gate_probe.sh, then asserts each probe omits exactly one required property of its class. Both sides are parsed rather than hardcoded, because a hardcoded copy is a second source of truth and drift here is invisible while the suite stays green. Two supporting tests: every arm targets a distinct shape, and each arm's expected term really is a required property of its class (an arm named for a property the shapes do not require would be refused for some other reason and still print PROVEN).

Verified the arithmetic: Decision requires sourceKind/label/chose; Verification sourceKind/label/falsifier; ExecutionPath sourceKind/label/executesArtifact/repositorySource/refreshedBy; Blocker sourceKind/label/blockerEvidence. Each probe omits exactly its target. The mandatory-label constraint is satisfied because a node's name becomes its rdfs:label — VERIFIED against quipu's own test rather than assumed (src/episode/tests.rs:742 asserts active_values(store, ns+'path-a', RDFS_LABEL) == ['path-a'] for a node written as {name: path-a}). That assumption is a named constant in the test so it goes red if it ever stops holding.

DYNAMIC HALF — GateSabotageTests, which is the sabotage the bead asked for. A SelectiveStore enforces EXACTLY ONE (class, property) shape and accepts everything else. Then: enforce gate i with arm i first, assert PROVEN (the positive half); and for every j != i, enforce gate i with arm j first and assert the arm reports ACCEPTED. That second test is what actually establishes independence — if arm j reported PROVEN, gate i's refusal would be standing in for gate j and a disabled gate j would look enforced. Plus a floor test: with nothing enforced, the first arm must report the gate is off, otherwise the whole suite could be passing against a store that refuses for unrelated reasons.

THE TESTS ARE PROVEN NON-VACUOUS, which is the bead's own discipline applied to the bead's own work. Two deliberate sabotages, both confirmed red:
  - Removed sourceKind from the falsifier probe so it violates two shapes: the static test fails with 'the falsifier arm omits [falsifier, sourceKind]'.
  - Made SelectiveStore refuse every write: 13 failures across GateSabotageTests, the store's blanket refusal correctly caught as arms that cannot tell their own gate from another's.

Suite 52 passed (was 46), just check 0 issues. Worth a sentence in the paper as section 5 of docs/design/paper.md notes: this is the thesis applied to the installer that enforces the thesis.

title: paper: fix the thesis boundary with the yupana paper before either drafts
description: Both papers instantiate one principle — a check that cannot fail is not a check, and absence of a finding is not a finding of absence. If both claim it, reviewers see one idea published twice and both papers weaken. Proposed split, to be agreed and written down in both plan docs: camayoc owns ADMISSION — what may enter the graph at all, provenance-refusing ingress, falsifier-gated verification, and the incident-night corpus showing what happens when verification is unfalsifiable. yupana owns the GUARD'S NON-ANSWERS at the action boundary — vacuous vs pass, unevaluated vs skipped, served_from_cache vs fail_open, unknown vs unsatisfied. Same principle, different layer, and each paper cites the other for the layer it does not own. Do this before drafting; retrofitting a boundary after two drafts exist is much harder.
acceptance_criteria: A stated boundary in both docs/design/paper.md files, each citing the other.
close_reason:
Done, and written down on BOTH sides as the bead required: docs/design/thesis-boundary.md here, mirrored as a new section 2.1 in yupana/docs/design/paper.md.

The bead's proposed split is adopted essentially as written — camayoc owns ADMISSION (provenance-refusing ingress, falsifier-gated verification, the closed source-tier vocabulary, the incident corpus); yupana owns THE GUARD'S NON-ANSWERS at the action boundary (vacuous vs pass, unevaluated vs skipped, served_from_cache vs fail_open, unknown vs unsatisfied, empty-board refusal, STALE-with-AGE). Added one thing the bead implied but did not state: NEITHER paper claims the shared principle as a contribution, because it is older than both systems. Each contributes a layer and the mechanisms that layer required, and each cites the other.

READING THE TWO PLAN DOCS AGAINST EACH OTHER FOUND TWO COLLISIONS THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE. The split is not self-executing without resolving them.

(1) yupana's paper plan section 4 already describes CAMAYOC'S MECHANISM as its own: 'the installer proving each refusal gate with deliberately invalid probes that each omit exactly one required property, so the arms discriminate'. That is scripts/gate_probe.sh and tests/test_gate_probe.py, in this repo, and proving the arms discriminate is camayoc-104. Resolution: camayoc owns it (the probes prove ADMISSION gates — the admission thesis applied to camayoc's own installer), yupana cites it. Also agreed that camayoc adopts yupana's existing term 'non-vacuity' rather than minting a second name for one idea. Both changes recorded in yupana's 2.1 as corrections its draft must make.

(2) Both systems report coverage as Empty|Partial|Full — camayoc for ontology reach, yupana for dataset population. Resolution: no exclusivity needed, because neither claims the shape as novel; different objects, and each cites the other as an independent instance. Two systems converging on one reporting shape from different directions is evidence FOR the principle.

Also recorded what the boundary costs camayoc, since the trade is real: handing over the non-answer taxonomy gives up the most immediately legible material (ten crisp distinctions, each forced by an incident). Justified because camayoc's typed non-answers are ONE instance while yupana's are a systematic taxonomy with per-distinction provenance — the stronger claim belongs where the stronger evidence is — and because camayoc retains the thing neither sibling can claim, the incident-night corpus.

Status: proposed and written on both sides; keeper sign-off pending. Flagged in the doc that if the two ever disagree, neither paper should draft until reconciled.

title: Settled-decision collision: similarity-check new Decision episodes against crew:declared before the write
description: quipu docs/design/semantic-grounded-edit-policies.md, Further applications #2. Before an agent's Decision episode lands, compare its embedding against standing human decisions in crew:declared; a match above threshold surfaces 'duplicates or conflicts with a settled decision' as advisory or escalation BEFORE the write. Convention memory made enforceable: the store notices re-litigation. Same disciplines: score/threshold/model/corpus-watermark in the verdict, nonzero OperatingPoint, advisory/escalate only, recorded facts land sourceKind=inferred. Depends on the quarantine planes existing (camayoc-s0h) and the grounding vocabulary (quipu-3aj, quipu tracker).
notes:
BLOCKED 2026-08-17 (Claude): depends on camayoc-s0h, which is now measured-blocked on two specific quipu gaps (no graph targeting on /knot, no label-set route) -- see s0h's notes for citations. Also depends on the grounding vocabulary (quipu-3aj). Building the similarity check before the planes exist would land its inferred verdicts in the same plane as observed facts, which is the exact thing it is meant to prevent.

RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-17 (Claude): still blocked, on the same two dependencies. camayoc-s0h (quarantine planes) was re-verified this pass and remains blocked on quipu; the grounding vocabulary (quipu-3aj) is unchanged.

The reason to keep holding is worth restating because it is not merely sequencing: building the similarity check before the planes exist would land its INFERRED verdicts in the same plane as OBSERVED facts. That is precisely the failure this bead's own discipline is meant to prevent — a model-written 'this duplicates a settled decision' judgment sitting at equal trust with a recorded human decision. Shipping it early would make the bead an instance of the thing it guards against.

Noted for whoever picks it up: the sibling scorer camayoc-b6h is partially implemented with a DETERMINISTIC matcher and no model (method='lexical-jaccard-v1', semantic=false, and a test forbidding the label from implying meaning-awareness). That is the pattern to follow here too if this ships before embeddings are available — a lexical first pass that says exactly what it is, rather than a semantic claim the implementation cannot support. b6h's embedding half is itself still blocked: re-tested this pass, the model weights still 403 on CONNECT.
close_reason:
Implemented as scripts/settled_decisions.py, now that camayoc-s0h landed and the planes exist.

WHAT IT DOES. Scores a proposed Decision against the standing human decisions exported from crew:declared. Above the advisory threshold it surfaces 'this may duplicate or conflict with a settled decision', naming the match, its score, and WHO decided it — a collision the reader cannot attribute is not actionable, since the whole point is to send them to the person who settled it. Two levels, advisory and escalate, as the bead specifies. Stage-1 posture throughout: advisory only, never blocks a write, never edits a decision.

DISCIPLINES THE BEAD REQUIRES, all present: score, threshold, method and corpus watermark in every verdict; nonzero operating point (advisory 0.20, escalate 0.45, both carried in the verdict so a reader can re-score and disagree); recorded facts land sourceKind=inferred.

METHOD HONESTY, inherited from camayoc-b6h on purpose. The scorer is LEXICAL and every verdict says semantic=false and method='lexical-jaccard-v1'. A test forbids the method label from containing any word mistakable for meaning-awareness. That is this repo's own rule turned on its own tooling: a lexical match must never be presented as a semantic one, exactly as an inferred fact must never masquerade as an observed one. It reuses competency.py's tokenizer and scorer rather than writing a second one — two similarity implementations in one repo drift, and the drift is invisible because both keep returning plausible numbers.

Thresholds set HIGHER than competency's floor, deliberately: the cost of a false positive differs. A spurious ontology gap files a bead; a spurious collision tells someone their new decision was already settled, which is a claim about a person.

WHY THIS NEEDED THE PLANES, which is what the earlier BLOCKED note got right. The recorded verdict is a MODEL-ADJACENT JUDGMENT ABOUT A HUMAN'S DECISION. verdict_episode routes it to crew:inferred and tags it inferred, and a test asserts it is NOT the declared plane. Writing a collision verdict into crew:declared beside the decision it comments on would make a machine's opinion indistinguishable from the human's statement — precisely the masquerade this bead was meant to guard against, committed by the guard itself. The verdict also names its own falsifier ('a human re-scores against the same corpus watermark and disagrees'), applying camayoc's shape rule to camayoc's own output.

no_corpus IS KEPT DISTINCT FROM clear. Scoring against zero settled decisions produces no matches and would otherwise render exactly like a clean result — the same collapse the gate probe, the coverage reporter and bobbin's bead advisory each had to unpick this session.

14 tests, including a control asserting an unrelated proposal comes back clear — without it every collision test could pass because everything collides.

Suite 107 passed (was 93); just check 0 issues.

title: camayoc: the git ingress feeds the only live rung of yupana's containment ladder — confirm coverage or it advises on nothing
description:
docs/design/ingress.md:203-205 claims the git adapter: 'Commit history -> work-item linkage (aegis:implements, aegis:modifies — the provenance chain quipu's co-occurrence shapes already define). Pure observed.'

That chain is load-bearing for three consumers outside this repo, and none of them owns it:

- yupana's WORK_ITEM_SCOPE_QUERY (src/project_queries.rs:131-137) walks `?c aegis:implements ?w ; aegis:modifies ?e . ?w aegis:identifier ?id . ?e aegis:filePath ?path` to build the OBSERVED scope rung — the only rung that exists, since declared and derived are still design intent.
- yupana's work-item briefing (src/brief_sources.rs) reads it for the item's ground.
- quipu's entity_work and cochanged_with named queries traverse it, and quipu's own src/mcp/named_query.rs carries the caveat that they 'return nothing until Phase-4 promotion populates the modifies/implements edges'.

So: the ingress cadence is the containment scope's freshness bound, and a repository that adapter does not cover produces UNKNOWN SCOPE for every agent working in it — which advises once and then allows silently, correctly but uselessly.

WHAT IS NEEDED: confirm whether the git adapter is implemented and running, for which repositories, at what cadence; and if it is not, say so explicitly rather than leaving downstream consumers to infer emptiness as 'nothing in scope'. yupana already distinguishes these two states on its side (an absent work_item_scopes map means unknown-scope-advises, deliberately not an empty map that would read as 'nothing is in scope') — the graph side should be equally legible.

ACCEPTANCE: a stated, checkable answer to 'which repositories have implements/modifies coverage, as of when'.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 from the yupana side while planning work-item containment. Not a request to change the boundary — docs/design/thesis-boundary.md puts admission here and action in yupana, and this bead respects that.

title: camayoc: progressive disclosure across the stack must not flatten the trust planes — the envelope rule is the pattern
description:
quipu, yupana and bobbin are gaining a disclosure ladder: a small pushed briefing that states how much it withheld, and expansion calls that return the rest. Summarising many facts into a count is exactly where plane attribution gets lost — a census line reading '4 similar work items' when three of them came from crew:inferred presents quarantined, model-inferred material at the same standing as canonical record. That is the masquerade this repo's ingress discipline exists to prevent, committed by the retrieval layer rather than the write layer.

The planes make the stakes concrete: crew:declared rank 30, crew:records 20, crew:inferred 0, and scripts/planes.py:49-52 records that the 20-to-0 gap is deliberate — 'a promotion out of quarantine should have to cross visible distance, not increment'. competency/crew-task-lifecycle.md Q14 already asks the question a flattened census would make unanswerable: what knowledge about a topic exists ONLY in the inferred plane, i.e. would vanish under a high-trust floor.

THE PATTERN TO REUSE, already written here: docs/patents/provisional-grounding-cluster.md sec 7 states the ENVELOPE RULE — the tier rides the response envelope, not merely the items, so an empty or not-found answer still declares the tier at which nothing was found. sec 8 adds typed non-answers, including verification-with-unchecked-disclosure (a verdict returns the violation classes it did NOT check, so a pass is a bounded claim) and the warning against an aggregate boolean, 'so no caller can read one bit and skip the outcomes that were never asked'.

Applied to disclosure: every level carries plane and trust ON THE ENVELOPE, and no level collapses to a single number that hides which plane it counted.

RELATED CONSTRAINT worth adopting at the same time, from quipu's knowledge packs (quipu/docs/design/knowledge-packs.md sec 3): 'a pack recommends; the consumer's config enforces'. A disclosure level may declare what it contains; it must not decide what a consumer is allowed to see.

ACCEPTANCE: this is a constraint to hold implementers to, not code here. Close it when the disclosure surfaces in quipu/yupana/bobbin carry plane+trust on their envelopes.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 from the yupana/quipu side. No terms are minted by the disclosure work — the counts and handles are wire fields on HTTP/MCP responses — so no camayoc gate is triggered.
close_reason: Held to, and the constraint is now discharged rather than pending. Every disclosure surface that shipped reports its omission ON THE ENVELOPE, per the §7 envelope rule: quipu's KnowledgeSummary.truncated (entities_considered / more_available / entities_with_more_facts, deliberately not shown/of because the walk stops at the budget), bobbin's omitted= header plus an explicit marker at the point of a budget cut, and yupana's L0 census with a per-section count and the call that expands it. Each has a both-outcomes test including the uncut case, because a report that cannot say 'nothing was withheld' is not a report. The plane/trust half remains a live constraint on the quipu_ask rungs rather than a shipped feature — noted on quipu-1uq, not lost.

title: Cover path-scoped policy boundaries: reuse aegis:appliesTo, add a competency question if needed
description: quipu now declares aegis:appliesTo (multi-valued repo-relative path globs scoping where an action-boundary policy binds) and ships a tripwire catalog — path-boundary policies with no selector/predicate (quipu shapes/policies/tripwire.ttl, main 0ae7e88; enforced by yupana main 9b736fa). Camayoc's disciplines both apply: (1) reuse-before-minting — any future camayoc ingress rule that scopes facts or rules by path must reuse aegis:appliesTo, never mint a camayoc: equivalent; (2) competency-questions-before-classes — if camayoc's suite ever needs to ask 'which boundaries govern writes touching X', add the question to competency/ referencing the aegis terms rather than new ones. This bead is the evaluation, not a mandate: close with 'no camayoc term needed' if the suite never asks the question.
close_reason: Evaluated 2026-08-25: NO CAMAYOC TERM NEEDED, and no competency question needs aegis:appliesTo today. The bead framed itself as an evaluation, not a mandate, and this is the outcome it named. FINDING. aegis:appliesTo appears nowhere in camayoc — not in ontology/core.ttl, not in shapes/, not in queries/, not in competency/. Reading the whole suite (91 questions, six slices, sha256:65bc4c5ad3d84752) against it, exactly two questions carry an <area> parameter and neither defines <area> as a repo-relative path: crew-task-lifecycle Q6 'What standing (declared) conventions apply to <area>?' and verification-and-liveness Q2 'Which verifications in <area> carry no falsifier?'. Q2's stored query (camayoc_verifications_without_falsifier) has params: [] and drops <area> entirely, so the parameter is unbound in practice as well as undefined in the suite; and a verification attaches to its subject via aegis:verifies, which is a graph join, not a path glob. Q6 is the nearer fit but is blocked one step earlier: camayoc has no standing-convention subject at all, and the coverage table added today (scripts/coverage_tables.py, crew-task-lifecycle Q6) registers it as a competency GAP whose open decision is whether to reuse quipu's aegis:Policy. Path scoping is downstream of a decision nobody has made. Deciding that <area> means a path glob because a term for path globs exists would be answering from the nearest available term — the adjacency defect the incident corpus catalogues — so the answer is no, not yet. BOTH DISCIPLINES UPHELD, NEITHER VIOLATED. (1) reuse-before-minting: recorded as a standing constraint rather than dropped, since a closed bead is where knowledge goes to be forgotten. aegis:appliesTo is now listed in the reuse table at docs/design/bootstrap-ontology.md §1 with an explicit note that camayoc uses it nowhere and that any future path-scoped rule reuses it rather than minting a camayoc: equivalent. (2) competency-questions-before-classes: no question was added to manufacture a need. If the suite ever asks 'which boundaries govern writes touching X', that question is written first, referencing the aegis terms, and this bead can be re-filed against it.

title: cost ingest: verify a codex rollout reader against a real rollout file before writing one
description: scripts/ingest_session_usage.py parses the claude harness layout and abstains on everything else. competency/verification-and-liveness.md section D names TWO harnesses; the codex layout (~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl, input/cached_input/cache_write/output/reasoning_output/total) is recorded there as prose only, and no real rollout file was available to measure a reader against when the parser was built. A parser written from a format description is a guess: the claude reader's central finding - that the unit of consumption is the API request, not the log entry, because one turn's usage object repeats on every content-block entry, a 2.5x overcount if summed naively - is exactly the kind of thing a field list does not tell you. Until a real rollout file can be read, codex logs are counted as UNRECOGNISED in the run's denominator and emit nothing, so codex consumption is ABSENT from every Q16-Q21 total rather than zero. Acceptance: obtain a real rollout-*.jsonl; determine empirically whether its usage entries repeat per turn and what the deduplication key is; add a reader to READERS with tests pinning the measured answer (including a control that would fail under the naive per-entry sum); update tests/test_ingest_session_usage.py::test_only_verified_formats_have_readers, which is deliberately written to break when READERS grows.
